skill.name: use-conductor
skill.description: Use conductor files to find project context, active tracks, workflow rules, and the next planned task.
skill.summary: Read conductor project files before starting work.
skill.author: 89jobrien

security_audit.summary: All static command-execution detections are markdown backticks, code fences, file names, or checklist markers in SKILL.md. I found no command execution, network calls, prompt injection, or reconnaissance intent. The blocker finding on line 69 is a false match on the `[~]` task status marker.

static_findings.snippet: Scan the `conductor/` directory at project root for structured project management files that provide
| `product.md` | Product vision, target audience, core features |
| `product-guidelines.md` | Naming conventions, quality standards, documentation rules |
| `workflow.md` | TDD methodology, task workflow, commit guidelines |
| `tracks.md` | High-level index of all work tracks |
| `tracks/<name>/spec.md` | Goals, scope, and success criteria for the track |
1. Check if `conductor/` directory exists at project root
3. For active tracks (marked `[~]`), read the track's `plan.md` to find current tasks
4. Follow the workflow methodology defined in `workflow.md`
1. **Respect the plan** - Follow the task order in `plan.md`
2. **Update status** - Mark tasks as `[~]` when starting, `[x]` when done
5. **Stay in scope** - Check `spec.md` for what's in/out of scope

content.value_statement: Project context is often scattered across planning files. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to read conductor files before work begins.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether a conductor directory exists at the project root.
Reads core conductor files for product direction, standards, and active work.
Identifies active tracks marked with the in-progress status marker.
Finds current tasks from track plan files.
Applies workflow guidance from conductor workflow documentation.
Uses conductor status markers when updating task progress.
limitations: Works only when a project includes conductor files.
Depends on the accuracy of the project planning documents.
Does not create a project plan unless the user asks.
Does not replace direct user instructions or repository policies.

use_cases.title: Find the next planned task
use_cases.description: Read active conductor tracks and identify the next unchecked task before starting implementation.

use_cases.title: Follow repository workflow rules
use_cases.description: Load workflow and guideline files so coding work follows the project process.

use_cases.title: Understand project direction quickly
use_cases.description: Review product and track documents to summarize project goals and current work.

prompt_templates.title: Check for conductor context
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this project has conductor files and summarize the key context before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find my next task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the conductor plan to find the active track and tell me the next task to work on.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the conductor workflow, active track plan, and relevant guidelines before implementing the selected task.

prompt_templates.title: Align work with conductor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conductor files to validate scope, workflow, and task status before editing code for the active track.

output_examples.input: What should I work on next?
output_examples.output: The active conductor track points to the next unchecked task. The summary includes the track goal, current status, and relevant workflow notes.
The agent reviews the conductor workflow, marks the task in progress when appropriate, and follows the documented project standards.

output_examples.input: Summarize the project before making changes.
output_examples.output: The response covers product purpose, active tracks, standards, and any workflow rules found in conductor files.

best_practices: Run the skill before starting work in an unfamiliar repository.
Keep conductor files current so task selection stays accurate.
Confirm the selected task with the user when the plan is ambiguous.
anti_patterns: Do not assume conductor files exist in every repository.
Do not ignore newer user instructions when conductor files are outdated.
Do not mark tasks complete before verification is finished.

faq.question: What is a conductor directory?
faq.answer: It is a project folder that stores product direction, workflow rules, and track plans.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions for reading planning files and following documented workflow.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What happens if conductor files are missing?
faq.answer: The agent should continue with normal repository discovery and user instructions.

faq.question: Can it update task status?
faq.answer: Yes, when appropriate. It uses the status markers documented in conductor plan files.

faq.question: Does it replace project documentation?
faq.answer: No. It depends on project documentation and helps the agent use it consistently.
